hygiene.title: Hygiene log — a sample for food service
hygiene.description: Hygiene log under SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26: automatic filling, work clearance, temperature checks and PDF for Rospotrebnadzor. 14 days free.
hygiene.seoIntro: The electronic food service hygiene log complies with SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26 and the Rospotrebnadzor order. Employee work clearance, symptoms and temperature, and the responsible person's signature are all on one screen, without paper or manual comparison with the timesheet.

health_check.title: Health log (ЗОЖ): conducting pre-shift checks
health_check.description: How to conduct daily pre-shift checks: who examines staff, which signs to record, when to remove someone from work and how to document refused clearance.
health_check.seoIntro: The health log is a detailed examination form. It records every symptom, not just work clearance, which is useful when investigating food poisoning. The electronic version records the examination time, removal from work and corrective actions.

climate_control.title: Premises temperature and humidity log
climate_control.description: Premises temperature and humidity log: sensors, automatic readings and ventilation schedules. Limits are set for each room; deviations go straight to the responsible person.
climate_control.seoIntro: A warehouse temperature and humidity log is a mandatory SanPiN item for rooms where food is stored: it confirms microclimate monitoring. In WeSetup, sensors take readings every 5–10 minutes, and deviations automatically go to CAPA.

cold_equipment_control.title: Refrigerator temperature log: limits and recordkeeping
cold_equipment_control.description: Temperature limits for refrigerators and freezers, how often to measure during a shift, who is responsible and what to do when readings leave the allowed range.
cold_equipment_control.seoIntro: The temperature log for refrigerators and freezers follows the form in Appendix No. 2 to SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26. Checking refrigerator temperatures is the daily minimum. WeSetup warns when the temperature leaves the allowed range and automatically creates a CAPA with the cause, responsible person and correction deadline.

cleaning_ventilation_checklist.title: Room airing checklist
cleaning_ventilation_checklist.description: Airing and ventilation checks in the kitchen and dining area: schedules, completion marks and supply/extract system maintenance. Missed intervals are immediately visible.
cleaning_ventilation_checklist.seoIntro: The airing checklist is a simple but often forgotten SanPiN item: kitchen air changes faster than dining-area air, so the schedules differ. The electronic template inserts standard values, reminds staff about frequency and stores results alongside the ventilation maintenance schedule.

cleaning.title: Cleaning log: how to keep it and who fills it in
cleaning.description: Who fills in the cleaning log, how often and what to record: room, product, concentration, contact time and supervisor. SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26 requirements.
cleaning.seoIntro: The cleaning log records every washing cycle for areas and utensils, including the cleaning product and concentration. The electronic form prevents a record from being closed with a required field missing, so the inspector always sees the complete picture.

general_cleaning.title: Deep cleaning schedule — an electronic log
general_cleaning.description: Plan and record deep cleaning: areas, products, responsible person and a signed report. Schedules cover the coming month; the system reminds you when work is due.
general_cleaning.seoIntro: Deep cleaning is a plan with dates and areas, not something left until there is time: kitchens, storage areas, dining areas and toilets are cleaned at different frequencies. WeSetup creates a monthly schedule, sends automatic reminders and generates a separate completion report for each area.

uv_lamp_runtime.title: UV lamp log — operation and operating hours
uv_lamp_runtime.description: Germicidal UV lamp log: operating hours, replacement date and safety. The 8000-9000 hour service life is counted automatically, with a reminder when it runs out.

keywords.item3: UV lamp service life in food service

uv_lamp_runtime.seoIntro: Recording germicidal UV lamp operation matters because a lamp can keep visibly glowing long after its service life ends, while its germicidal effect is already gone. WeSetup counts the hours automatically and warns about scheduled replacement; a sample completed log is available to download.

finished_product.title: Finished product quality checks: keeping the log
finished_product.description: Who sits on the food quality assessment panel, which sensory qualities to assess and which serving temperature to record. Recordkeeping under SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26.
finished_product.seoIntro: The finished product quality assessment log is a key food service log; it previously followed SanPiN 2.3.2.1324-03 and now follows 2.3/2.4.4282-26. WeSetup stores assessments separately for each batch, preventing morning and lunchtime baking from being combined into one record, as required for investigating a complaint.

perishable_rejection.title: Perishable product rejection log
perishable_rejection.description: Record rejected perishable products: sensory assessment, defects, reasons and actions taken. Every rejected batch is linked to a write-off.
perishable_rejection.seoIntro: Perishable products must be checked for rejection at goods acceptance and during the shift. The electronic log links the batch to its delivery note and subsequent records, allowing its path from supplier to table to be traced in 2–4 hours.

incoming_control.title: Raw material acceptance and incoming inspection log
incoming_control.description: Incoming raw material checks: temperature on receipt, packaging, expiry dates and supplier details. Integration with iiko and 1С loads the item list automatically.
incoming_control.seoIntro: Incoming inspection of raw materials and food is the first critical point in the HACCP system. WeSetup automatically loads delivery notes from iiko and 1С; the cook records the temperature on receipt and sensory assessment without copying supplier details by hand. A sample completed log can be downloaded and printed.

fryer_oil.title: Frying oil usage log
fryer_oil.description: Frying oil records: polar compound measurements, replacement schedule, disposal and collection report. At the 24% limit, the log reminds you to change the oil.
fryer_oil.seoIntro: Frying oil records are a simple but mandatory item. The 24% polar compound limit is checked with a handheld analyzer; WeSetup saves the reading, reminds you to change the oil and stores the contractor's disposal report.

med_books.title: Employee medical record book log — electronic records
med_books.description: Employee medical record books: renewals, chest X-rays and examinations. A reminder arrives 30 days before expiry, and expired work clearance is blocked.
med_books.seoIntro: The electronic medical record book log automatically reminds you a month before a chest X-ray or scheduled examination expires. This removes the risk of an inspector finding an expired document for an employee who is working.

training_plan.title: Staff training plan
training_plan.description: Annual food service staff training plan: topics, dates, responsible person and links to the briefing log. Completed training is marked with one click.
training_plan.seoIntro: The staff training plan links topics and dates to the briefing log. WeSetup automatically creates notifications about missing items when a new employee starts a shift.

staff_training.title: Staff briefing register
staff_training.description: Record completed briefings: topic, date and signatures of the instructor and employee. Kept for three years and exported for any inspection period.
staff_training.seoIntro: Keeping a briefing register is daily practice under the training requirements for staff involved in food production and circulation. The electronic signature saves the person's full name and timestamp automatically, and a sample completed form is available to download.

disinfectant_usage.title: Disinfectant usage log
disinfectant_usage.description: Disinfectant records: consumption, concentration, application area and contact time. DDD contractor reports sit alongside the records, so nothing has to be found for an inspection.
disinfectant_usage.seoIntro: The disinfection log, also known as disinfectant records, concerns consumption and concentration rather than floor washing. WeSetup records the product, volume, application area and waiting period before production resumes. DDD contractor reports for disinfection, insect control and rodent control are also stored here; a sample completed form can be downloaded and printed.

sanitary_day_control.title: Sanitation day checklist
sanitary_day_control.description: Sanitation day guidance and checklist: areas, products, completion report and management checks. Monthly reminders arrive automatically, and unfinished work appears in a list.
sanitary_day_control.seoIntro: A sanitation day is a scheduled production shutdown for deep cleaning. The WeSetup checklist includes all required areas and becomes a completed report for inspection.

equipment_maintenance.title: Equipment maintenance log
equipment_maintenance.description: Scheduled and unscheduled food service equipment maintenance: service visits, reports, frequency and links to equipment records. The next maintenance date is calculated automatically.
equipment_maintenance.seoIntro: The equipment maintenance log is linked to the equipment record, showing the last service date, interval and next scheduled date. Emergency repairs go into the breakdown log linked to CAPA.

breakdown_history.title: Equipment breakdown history log
breakdown_history.description: Equipment breakdown history: cause, repair, write-off and contractor report. Recurring failures are immediately visible, supporting replacement instead of another repair.
breakdown_history.seoIntro: The breakdown and fault history log helps identify patterns: which equipment fails most often, what downtime costs and whether replacement pays off. WeSetup stores contractor reports and defect photos directly in the record.

equipment_calibration.title: Equipment and thermometer verification log
equipment_calibration.description: Verification of thermometers, scales and measuring instruments: frequency, certificates and links to the metrology service. The system reminds you when verification is due.
equipment_calibration.seoIntro: Thermometer and scale verification is mandatory for production facilities supplying retail chains. Calibration and verification are different procedures: the former adjusts the instrument, while the latter confirms its accuracy with a document. WeSetup automatically calculates the next verification date and attaches a scanned certificate.

incoming_raw_materials_control.title: Raw material and semi-finished goods inspection log
incoming_raw_materials_control.description: Detailed incoming inspection: certificates, laboratory reports, temperature and labeling checks. Supplier documents are stored with the goods acceptance record.
incoming_raw_materials_control.seoIntro: Incoming inspection of raw materials and semi-finished products is a mandatory HACCP requirement. WeSetup stores the test report and certificate with the record, avoiding the common mistake of keeping the papers with the accountant and the record in the cook's folder.

ppe_issuance.title: Personal protective equipment issue log
ppe_issuance.description: Record personal protective equipment issued: gloves, coats, head coverings, workwear and employee signatures. Stock levels and issue frequency are calculated automatically.
ppe_issuance.seoIntro: The PPE issue log is required by both SanPiN and the labor inspectorate. The electronic form prevents signatures from being lost: the employee signs in the Telegram bot, and the entry reaches the log in seconds.

accident_journal.title: Accident and emergency log
accident_journal.description: Record accidents, incidents and corrective measures: circumstances, people affected and action taken. Every record links to a CAPA and an investigation report.
accident_journal.seoIntro: The accident log records all unplanned events, from power outages to cleaning product spills. A record cannot be closed without a corrective action.

complaint_register.title: Complaints and claims register
complaint_register.description: Record guest complaints: contact channel, issue, responsible person, response deadline and compensation. Overdue complaints are highlighted and causes collected in a report.
complaint_register.seoIntro: The complaints log is a simple way to avoid losing guest feedback. WeSetup routes the complaint to a manager; if it recurs, it automatically opens a CAPA with a responsible person and deadline.

daily_samples.title: Daily food sample log — electronic records
daily_samples.description: Daily food sample collection and storage log for schools, kindergartens and hospitals: dish, weight, sampling time, storage temperature and disposal. Print the log with one click.
daily_samples.seoIntro: The electronic daily food sample log lets the cook select the meal and dish; the sampling date and time are filled in automatically. The inspector sees that samples were taken from every dish and stored for the required period.

vitaminization.title: Vitamin fortification log for third-course dishes
vitaminization.description: Vitamin fortification of third-course and sweet dishes: preparation, portion count, vitamin added, addition and serving times. For children's and therapeutic meals.
vitaminization.seoIntro: The electronic vitamin fortification log takes a minute to fill in, and the time the vitamin was added and the dish served are always visible side by side, exactly what the inspector checks.

ration_control.title: Dietary intake control sheet
ration_control.description: Diet control sheet: required and actual food quantities per person over 10 days or a month, with percentage deviations. For children's and medical institutions.
ration_control.seoIntro: The diet control sheet shows where actual meals differ from the standard by food group and helps adjust the next period's menu.

transport_temperature.title: Transport temperature log
transport_temperature.description: Product temperature control during transport: vehicle, route, loading and unloading temperatures. For catering, delivery and food production facilities.
transport_temperature.seoIntro: The transport temperature log covers the critical delivery point: two readings on each trip confirm that the cold or hot chain was not broken.

tableware_breakage.title: Tableware breakage log
tableware_breakage.description: Record tableware breakage in restaurants, cafés and canteens: what broke, where, why and whether fragments were collected. Physical hazard protection and clear loss statistics.
tableware_breakage.seoIntro: The tableware breakage log records every incident immediately, with the cause and confirmation that fragments were collected. It shows both the risk to guests and where breakages occur most often.

pool_water_control.title: Swimming pool water monitoring log
pool_water_control.description: Pool water quality log: temperature, free and combined chlorine, pH, clarity and visitor count. For fitness centers, sports clubs and hotels.
pool_water_control.seoIntro: The electronic pool water log lets the technician enter readings on a phone at the poolside. Deviations are immediately visible, and the inspection log prints with one click.

inventory_condition.title: Utensil condition assessment log
inventory_condition.description: Metal and plastic utensil condition log: inspection of knives, boards and containers, damage and removal from use. For kitchens and food production facilities.
inventory_condition.seoIntro: The electronic utensil condition log makes inspecting each board and spatula a matter of seconds, while damaged utensils are immediately visible and do not remain in the production area.

instrument_sterilization.title: Instrument sterilization monitoring log
instrument_sterilization.description: Instrument sterilization log for beauty salons and nail studios: method, cycle settings, indicator and sterilizer. Electronic records with printing for inspections.

keywords.item2: nail studio dry heat sterilizer log

instrument_sterilization.seoIntro: The electronic sterilization log lets the practitioner record a dry heat sterilizer or autoclave load from a phone, while the administrator sees that every cycle was completed with an indicator.

medical_waste_b.title: Class Б waste log
medical_waste_b.description: Class Б waste log: waste type and quantity, decontamination, packaging and handover to the collection organization. For salons offering cosmetology and medical practices.

keywords.item1: class Б waste in beauty salons

medical_waste_b.seoIntro: The class Б waste log traces every package from the treatment room to handover to the collection organization, without paper notebooks.

batch_release.title: Product batch release for shipment log
batch_release.description: Release finished product batches for shipment: batch number, quantity, sensory, labeling and packaging checks, and the responsible person's decision. For production and bakeries.
batch_release.seoIntro: The batch release log records who released the products and which checks preceded release. The batch number makes the record easy to find if a customer makes a claim.

product_writeoff.title: Product write-off log
product_writeoff.description: Write off expired, rejected or returned products: reason, weight and responsible person. Links to iiko and 1С inventory remove written-off items without duplicate entry.
product_writeoff.seoIntro: The product write-off log closes the gap between the warehouse and kitchen. Expiry write-offs reach iiko and 1С in real time, so the inspector sees the same stock on the shelf and in the record.

audit_plan.title: Internal audit plan and program
audit_plan.description: Annual HACCP internal audit plan: topics, frequency, auditors and links to audit records and reports. Missed audits are visible before an inspector asks about them.
audit_plan.seoIntro: The internal audit plan and program is the first document an auditor starts with. WeSetup creates the annual plan, assigns auditors and links every inspection to its audit record and report.

audit_protocol.title: Internal audit record
audit_protocol.description: Record the audit process: date, area, auditor, factual observations, nonconformities and evidence. The report and corrective actions are assembled from the record automatically.
audit_protocol.seoIntro: The internal audit record is the audit team's working document. WeSetup allows photographic evidence of nonconformities to be attached directly to the relevant record item.

audit_report.title: Internal audit report
audit_report.description: Final internal audit report: nonconformities with severity levels, CAPA, correction deadlines and the manager's signature. Overdue actions are highlighted.
audit_report.seoIntro: The internal audit report is a management document. The manager reads it and uses it to decide on CAPA and investments. WeSetup generates the report automatically from audit records and classifies nonconformities by severity.

traceability_test.title: Traceability test log
traceability_test.description: Periodic traceability test: a random batch, reconstructing its path from supplier to table and checking response time. The required window is two to four hours.
traceability_test.seoIntro: The traceability test is a quarterly exercise: for a randomly selected batch, the team must reconstruct the chain within 2–4 hours. WeSetup splits the chain into stages and automatically times each step.

metal_impurity.title: Metal contamination control log
metal_impurity.description: Metal contamination control log: metal detector checks, frequency, calibration and detection reports. Every detection is linked to the batch's disposition.
metal_impurity.seoIntro: Metal contamination control is required in food production. WeSetup records metal detector activations and periodic calibration, linking them to the instrument's maintenance reports.

equipment_cleaning.title: Equipment washing and disinfection log
equipment_cleaning.description: Washing and disinfection of slicers, mixers, ovens and ice makers: products, concentrations, contact time and swab tests. Equipment is the number one cross-contamination source.
equipment_cleaning.seoIntro: Equipment washing and disinfection has its own log because equipment is the number one source of cross-contamination. WeSetup inserts the selected product and counts the contact time automatically, preventing the disinfectant from being rinsed off too soon.

intensive_cooling.title: Rapid cooling log
intensive_cooling.description: Rapid cooling control for finished products: from +65 to +10 °C in two hours. Blast chiller, sensor and automatic report; excess time is recorded and sent to CAPA.
intensive_cooling.seoIntro: Rapid cooling of finished products is a HACCP critical point. Limit: +65 → +10 °C in 2 hours. WeSetup collects sensor readings in the blast freezer and generates a completed report.

glass_items_list.title: Glassware inventory log
glass_items_list.description: Kitchen glass item inventory: availability, quantities and regular integrity checks. Breakage or missing items are immediately linked to the glass control log.
glass_items_list.seoIntro: The glassware inventory log helps prevent fragments from entering a dish. WeSetup stores the list, and each inventory check shows that everything is in place.

glass_control.title: Glass control log
glass_control.description: Check glass and mirror integrity in production areas: record breakage, investigate and withdraw products. Every incident automatically creates a CAPA ticket.
glass_control.seoIntro: Glass control is a HACCP point in major production facilities. Every breakage incident opens a CAPA and links to the glass item inventory, so the inspector sees the complete control cycle.

pest_control.title: Disinfection, insect and rodent control log
pest_control.description: Scheduled DDD treatment records: contractor, product, site, waiting period and reports. The contract and reports sit beside the schedule, the first things an inspector requests.
pest_control.seoIntro: The disinfection, insect and rodent control log is mandatory for any thorough inspection. WeSetup attaches the contractor's report directly to the record and automatically blocks production during the waiting period after treatment.

publicJournalDetailFaq.fieldsAnswer: Required fields: {fields}. An empty field is equivalent to an incomplete log for an inspector, so use a dash deliberately and include an explanation.

cadence.sanpin_daily: Every shift: make the entry on the day of the event. Do not backdate entries: uniform dates and identical values are precisely how inspectors identify record keeping done only as a formality.
cadence.sanpin_periodic: According to the schedule, rather than daily: the frequency is set in the production control programme and must match the actual records.
cadence.haccp: According to the HACCP plan: the frequency is set when describing the control point and justified in the plan itself.

publicJournalDetailFaq.normativeAnswer: {norms}. Include the regulatory reference on the title page so the inspector can immediately see why the log is kept.
publicJournalDetailFaq.electronicAnswer: Yes. SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26 does not require paper: the important points are being able to see who made an entry and when, and preventing unnoticed retrospective changes. For an inspection, print the electronic log for the required period.
publicJournalDetailFaq.retentionAnswer: Inspectors usually request records for the last 12 months, so one year is a practical minimum. Keep logs connected with a food poisoning investigation or a complaint until the proceedings are closed.

guide.title: How checklists work
guide.typicalBody: Six ready-made inspections: SanPiN, HACCP, territorial manager, chief technologist, inspection readiness and HACCP team audit. “Add to organization” makes your own copy that you can edit in the builder.
guide.runBody: “Start inspection” opens the questions section by section. Answer them, attach photos where asked and press “Complete inspection”.
guide.assignBody: In “Assignments” a manager chooses who runs the inspection, how often, by what time and who accepts the result. A reminder arrives in Telegram.
guide.resultsBody: “Results” holds the inspection history: scores, violations, PDF and “Accept result”.
guide.q1: Will the standard checklist change if I edit my copy?
guide.a1: No. Your organization has its own copy: builder edits change only that copy.
guide.q2: Why don’t I see the “Add” button?
guide.a2: Managers add and edit templates. Anyone with write access to checklists can run inspections.

guide.title: How assignments work
guide.whoBody: A location means everyone working there; a position means all staff in that position; or a single person. Dismissed and deactivated staff are skipped.
guide.whenTitle: How often and by what time
guide.whenBody: Once, every day, weekly or monthly — by the set time in the organization’s time zone. One completed inspection per period is enough.
guide.remindBody: On the due day, 2 hours before the deadline, each recipient with a linked Telegram gets one message with an “Open checklist” button. Nothing is sent once the inspection is done.
guide.verifyBody: When the inspection is completed, the reviewer gets a message and presses “Accept result” in “Results”.
guide.q1: What happens when I pause an assignment?
guide.a1: No reminders are sent and the checklist doesn’t appear in “Assigned to you”. Resume it and it continues from the next deadline.
guide.a2: No. Checklist assignments live in WeSetup: reminders come from the WeSetup bot and no TasksFlow tasks are created.

hygieneHealthPdf.responsiblePosition: Position of the person responsible for monitoring
hygieneHealthPdf.results: This log records the results of:
hygieneHealthPdf.rosterReminder: The employees recorded in the log on the examination date must match the number of employees on the shift that day
hygieneHealthPdf.note0: examining employees and asking about their health (signs of respiratory and intestinal diseases and infections);
hygieneHealthPdf.note1: asking employees whether they have upper respiratory tract diseases or pustular skin diseases on their hands and exposed body areas;
hygieneHealthPdf.note2: asking employees about contact with people who have had gastrointestinal infections, people who are ill, and those returning from another country or a constituent region of the Russian Federation;
hygieneHealthPdf.note3: examining employees’ hands and exposed body areas for pustular diseases and damaged skin.
hygieneHealthPdf.legend1: DO – day off / leave / time off;
hygieneHealthPdf.legend2: SL – sick leave / suspended from work due to illness
hygieneHealthPdf.healthNote0: Every day, each employee who works in contact with food must sign to confirm that they have no diarrhoea, vomiting, jaundice, sore throat with fever, or similar cases in their family; no pus-containing lesions, such as boils and infected wounds on the hands and forearms, on or above the neck, or any other exposed body area; and no minor injuries, such as purulent or infected wounds on the wrists, forearms and exposed body areas. They must also confirm that family members have no intestinal diseases.
hygieneHealthPdf.healthNote1: To prevent coronavirus infection, employees must report contact with people who are ill and with people who have arrived from another region of the Russian Federation or another country within the last 14 days. All contacts must be suspended from work.
hygieneHealthPdf.healthReminder: Employees record their own checks using the hygiene log QR code before the shift — one check is recorded in both logs at once.

page.title: Promo codes
page.explanation: A subscription discount at checkout: a percentage or ruble amount, validity period and usage limit, with an optional new-customer restriction. Only paid orders count; an abandoned order does not use a redemption. If a promotion is active (ROOT → “Promotions”), the code is calculated from the promotional price. Equipment is not discounted. A “lifetime” code attaches the discount to the account after its first paid use and applies it automatically to later payments (discounts do not stack; the best one is used). A personal code works only for its specified email or organization. Starter codes are in {seedScript} (they are created inactive).

metadata.title: WeSetup Partner Programme
metadata.description: The WeSetup partner programme for SanPiN and HACCP consultants and integrators: manage clients in one workspace under your brand and earn rewards from subscriptions.

hero.title: Support your SanPiN and HACCP clients under your own brand
hero.body: One workspace for all your establishments: see whose logs are overdue, whose medical record books are expiring and where help is needed. Clients see your logo and contacts, while you receive {subscriptionPercent}% from subscriptions and {hardwarePercent}% from equipment.

consultants.title: SanPiN / HACCP consultants
consultants.body: Support several establishments: see their logs and overdue entries without calls or screenshots, and help during an inspection using “The inspector is here”.

integrators.title: Integrators and equipment services
integrators.body: Install sensors and tablets, connect the client to WeSetup and receive a share of subscriptions and equipment purchased through you.

chains.title: Chains and management companies
chains.body: Your own brand at sign-in and in the workspace, an overview of every location and separate access for your team members.

workspace.title: Partner workspace
workspace.body: An overview of clients: active clients, logs overdue today and medical record books expiring within the next 30 days. A profile for each client with notes only you can see.

branding.title: White-label branding
branding.body: A logo, accent colour, sign-in greeting, PDF signature and a “Your consultant” section in the workspace, emails and Telegram bot. The “{platformBadge}” attribution remains.

pageCode.title: Your page and code
pageCode.body: wesetup.ru/p/'<your-address>' and a six-digit code: the client registers through the link or enters the code in settings and is immediately linked to you.

clientAccess.title: The client controls access
clientAccess.body: The client chooses “view only” or “edit” access and can change the level or disconnect you at any time. All your actions in their workspace appear in the audit log.

invitations.title: Invitations
invitations.body: Ready-to-use Telegram and email messages, and email invitations with “sent / registered / declined” statuses.

rewards.title: Transparent rewards
rewards.body: Every accrual is linked to a client payment. Monthly totals, CSV export, payment details and agreement status are in one section.

rewards.title: Rewards
rewards.ruleVersion: Current rules: version {version}. Rules are versioned: each accrual retains the version used to calculate it, and a new version does not recalculate earlier accruals.

subscription.label: of every subscription payment
subscription.body: for the {subscriptionMonths}-month period from the client's first payment

hardware.label: of the equipment price

bonus.label: one-off bonus
bonus.body: after subscription payment number {bonusAfterPayments} by the client

rewards.note1: Example: Standard billed monthly at {subscriptionRub} → {subscriptionRewardRub} to the partner for every payment.
rewards.note3: A client refund reverses the same amount. Monthly accruals become “payable” on the 1st of the following month.
rewards.note4: The minimum payout is {minPayoutRub}; a smaller amount carries over to the following month.

application.title: Apply
application.body: Company name, tax ID, type, city, telephone, the number of establishments you support and your page address. Submit the application from your organisation settings in WeSetup.

review.title: Review
review.body: We review applications manually, usually within one or two working days. You will receive a reply by email and in Telegram.

launch.title: Launch
launch.body: Three steps in the workspace: logo and contacts, invitation link and payment details. Payments begin after the agreement is signed.

agreement.title: Partner agreement — main provisions
agreement.summary: The full text is in the <agreementLink>partner programme agreement</agreementLink>. WeSetup marks the agreement as signed; until then, accruals accumulate but are not paid out.
agreement.clause1: A partner is a legal entity, individual entrepreneur or self-employed person who has passed verification. The partner is not a representative of WeSetup and does not enter into agreements on its behalf; the offer and client prices remain unchanged.
agreement.clause2: A client connects to a partner only through their own action: a link, code or invitation. An organisation can have no more than one partner at a time; the partner's own organisation cannot be their client.
agreement.clause3: The client chooses the access level for their workspace (“view only” or “edit”) and can change or revoke it at any time. The partner uses access only to support the client and does not transfer it to third parties.
agreement.clause4: Rewards accrue under the version of the rules effective at the time of payment ({subscriptionPercent}% from subscriptions for the {subscriptionMonths}-month period, {hardwarePercent}% from equipment and a bonus of {bonusAmountRub} after payment number {bonusAfterPayments}). A client refund reverses the accrual.
agreement.clause5: Monthly accruals become “payable” on the 1st of the following month. A payout is made when the amount is at least {minPayoutRub}, using the payment details in the workspace, after the agreement is signed; a smaller amount carries over.
agreement.clause6: White-label branding covers the logo, colour, greeting, contacts and signature; the “{platformBadge}” attribution is not removed. The partner warrants their rights to uploaded materials.
agreement.clause7: The partner is not an employee or officer of the referred client, does not participate in that client's procurement decision and does not pass rewards to the client's employees (anti-corruption clause, 273-ФЗ).
agreement.clause8: WeSetup may suspend the partnership following a breach of the terms or client complaints: branding is removed, workspace access is closed and accruals cease; the accumulated history is retained.

document.title: Privacy and Personal Data Processing Policy
document.intro: This document explains which personal data ООО «БФС» processes when the wesetup.ru website, WeSetup web application and Telegram Mini App are used, the grounds for processing, how long the data is retained and how a personal data subject can exercise their rights.

publicPrivacy.clause1_1: 1.1. This Privacy and Personal Data Processing Policy (the “Policy”) establishes the procedure for processing and protecting the personal data of individuals using wesetup.ru and its related services.
publicPrivacy.clause1_2: 1.2. The Policy has been developed in accordance with the Constitution of the Russian Federation, Federal Law No. 152-ФЗ of 27.07.2006 “On Personal Data” (“152-ФЗ”), Federal Law No. 149-ФЗ of 27.07.2006 “On Information, Information Technologies and Information Protection”, and other regulatory legal acts of the Russian Federation concerning personal data protection.
publicPrivacy.clause1_3: 1.3. The personal data operator is Общество с ограниченной ответственностью «БФС» (the “Operator”, “Company”, “we”), INN 5018215599, OGRN 1235000105306, address: 141065, Московская область, г. Королёв, ул. Ленина, д. 10/6.
publicPrivacy.clause1_4: 1.4. The Policy applies to all personal data the Operator receives from users when they use wesetup.ru, the WeSetup web application and Telegram Mini App through @wesetupbot.
publicPrivacy.clause1_5: 1.5. This Policy is a publicly available document published openly on wesetup.ru.
publicPrivacy.clause1_6: 1.6. Use of the Services constitutes the User's agreement with this Policy and the personal data processing conditions stated in it. If the User disagrees with the Policy, they must stop using the Services.
publicPrivacy.clause2_1: 2.1. Personal data means any information relating to an identified or identifiable individual, directly or indirectly (a personal data subject).
publicPrivacy.clause2_2: 2.2. Personal data processing means any action or set of actions performed on personal data, including collection, recording, systematisation, accumulation, storage, clarification (updating, modification), retrieval, use, transfer (provision, access), anonymisation, blocking, deletion and destruction.
publicPrivacy.clause2_3: 2.3. Operator means ООО «БФС», which independently or jointly with others organises and/or carries out personal data processing and determines its purposes, the personal data to be processed and the actions performed on it.
publicPrivacy.clause2_4: 2.4. User means an individual using the Operator's Services: a website visitor, a registered web application user or a Telegram Mini App user.
publicPrivacy.clause2_5: 2.5. Client means a legal entity or individual entrepreneur that has entered into an agreement with the Operator to use the Services and created an organisation (account) in WeSetup.
publicPrivacy.clause2_6: 2.6. Services means wesetup.ru, the WeSetup web application (electronic SanPiN/HACCP logs for catering establishments and food production facilities), and Telegram Mini App available through @wesetupbot.
publicPrivacy.clause2_7: 2.7. Cookies are small text files placed by a website in the User's browser to store session and settings data.
publicPrivacy.clause2_8: 2.8. Electronic logs are accounting documents (records) created by the Client and its employees in the Services to comply with sanitary legislation and HACCP principles.

section3.title: 3. Legal grounds for personal data processing
section3.item1: the personal data subject's consent to processing their personal data (clause 1, part 1, article 6 of 152-ФЗ), expressed during registration, subscription or other use of the Services;
section3.item2: performance of an agreement to which the personal data subject is a party, beneficiary or guarantor (clause 5, part 1, article 6 of 152-ФЗ);
section3.item3: the Client's instruction to the Operator to process personal data, with the Client acting as the personal data operator for its employees (part 3, article 6 of 152-ФЗ);
section3.item4: performance of obligations imposed on the Operator by Russian Federation legislation, including tax and accounting legislation (clause 2, part 1, article 6 of 152-ФЗ);
section3.item5: exercise of the Operator's rights and legitimate interests, provided that the personal data subject's rights and freedoms are not infringed (clause 7, part 1, article 6 of 152-ФЗ).

publicPrivacy.clause3_1: 3.1. The Operator processes personal data on the following legal grounds:
publicPrivacy.clause3_2: 3.2. The Operator does not process personal data authorised by the subject for dissemination.
publicPrivacy.clause4_1: 4.1. The Operator processes personal data solely for the following purposes:
publicPrivacy.clause4_1_1: 4.1.1. Registering and identifying the User in the Services and providing access to the personal workspace and web application features.
publicPrivacy.clause4_1_2: 4.1.2. Entering into, performing and terminating an agreement for access to the Services, including subscribing and extending the subscription period.
publicPrivacy.clause4_1_3: 4.1.3. Maintaining electronic SanPiN/HACCP logs on the Client's instructions, including creating, storing, displaying and exporting log records.
publicPrivacy.clause4_1_4: 4.1.4. Enabling Telegram Mini App to operate: authorising the User and sending task notifications and reminders.
publicPrivacy.clause4_1_5: 4.1.5. Processing payments for the Services, including recording the fact, amount and period of payment and preparing closing documents.
publicPrivacy.clause4_1_6: 4.1.6. Providing technical support to Users and Clients and responding to enquiries sent to <supportLink>support@wesetup.ru</supportLink>.
publicPrivacy.clause4_1_7: 4.1.7. Improving the Services, analysing user behaviour in anonymised or aggregated form, correcting technical errors and ensuring information security.
publicPrivacy.clause4_1_8: 4.1.8. Informing Users about changes to the Services, prices, service terms and this Policy.
publicPrivacy.clause4_1_9: 4.1.9. Complying with Russian Federation legislation, including maintaining accounting and tax records.
publicPrivacy.clause4_2: 4.2. The Operator does not use personal data for purposes incompatible with those listed above and does not make decisions producing legal consequences for the subject solely on the basis of automated personal data processing.
publicPrivacy.clause5_1: 5.1. User account data: surname, first name and patronymic; email address; mobile telephone number; position and role in the organisation; password (stored solely as an irreversible cryptographic hash; the Operator cannot access the plain-text password).
publicPrivacy.clause5_2: 5.2. Client organisation data: legal entity or individual entrepreneur name, tax ID, registered and actual addresses, bank and other details, and responsible persons' contact details.
publicPrivacy.clause5_3: 5.3. Electronic log records, which may contain: surnames, first names and patronymics of the Client's employees; health and hygiene marks (including examination results, fitness-for-work marks and signs of illness); temperature readings for premises, equipment and products; other production and monitoring indicators required by sanitary legislation and the Client's HACCP plan; the date and time of an entry and information about the person who made it.
publicPrivacy.clause5_4: 5.4. Photo attachments to electronic log records, uploaded by Users as documentary evidence of measures carried out (the condition of premises, equipment and products, and instrument readings).
publicPrivacy.clause5_5: 5.5. Telegram data when Telegram Mini App is used: Telegram ID, username, first name and surname in the Telegram profile, interface language, and the chat identifier for sending notifications.
publicPrivacy.clause5_6: 5.6. Technical data: IP address; cookies; browser and operating system information; device type and parameters; screen resolution; the date, time and duration of access to the Services; referring pages; data from the Яндекс.Метрика web analytics system, including “Вебвизор” technology (recording user actions in the interface: cursor movements, clicks, scrolling and form completion, without storing the content of password or payment-data input fields).
publicPrivacy.clause5_7: 5.7. Payment data: the fact of payment, payment amount, date and time, paid plan and subscription period, and transaction status.
publicPrivacy.clause5_8: 5.8. The Operator does not receive, process or store Users' bank card data. Bank card details are entered and processed directly on the secure page of the payment service “Робокасса” (ООО «Бизнес-Процессинг»), certified to the PCI DSS security standard. The Operator receives only payment-result information from the payment service.
publicPrivacy.clause5_9: 5.9. The Operator does not process biometric personal data or special categories of personal data concerning racial or ethnic origin, political views, religious or philosophical beliefs, or intimate life. Health information is processed solely as fitness-for-work marks required by sanitary legislation and only on the Client's instructions. An employee's sign-in on the Client's shared device is photographed (a camera frame when identity is confirmed by PIN) only if the Client enables this feature and the employee consents; the frame is stored as evidence that a record was signed, and no automatic facial recognition or other biometric technologies are applied to it.
publicPrivacy.clause5_10: 5.10. The Operator does not deliberately collect minors' personal data. The Services are intended for people who have reached an age permitting them to enter into employment and contractual relationships.

section6.title: 6. Methods and periods of personal data processing
section6.item1: User account data and Client data are stored for the term of the agreement and 3 (three) years after its termination, or until consent is withdrawn, unless otherwise required by law;
section6.item2: electronic log records and photo attachments are stored for the period set by the Client and by sanitary legislation governing retention of accounting documentation, but for no less than 12 months;
section6.item3: payment data and accounting documents are stored for no less than 5 (five) years in accordance with tax legislation and the Federal Law “On Accounting”;
section6.item4: technical data and web analytics data are stored in anonymised form for no more than 25 months.

publicPrivacy.clause6_1: 6.1. Personal data is processed using automated means and without such means, including collection, recording, systematisation, accumulation, storage, clarification, retrieval, use, transfer, anonymisation, blocking, deletion and destruction.
publicPrivacy.clause6_2: 6.2. Personal data is collected through: the User's own data entry during registration and use of the Services; receipt of data from the Client when employee accounts are created; receipt of data from Telegram during authorisation through Telegram Mini App; and automatic collection of technical data when the Services are accessed.
publicPrivacy.clause6_4: 6.4. When processing purposes have been achieved or are no longer necessary, personal data must be destroyed or anonymised within no more than 30 days, unless otherwise provided by law or the agreement.
publicPrivacy.clause6_5: 6.5. When the personal data subject withdraws consent to processing, the Operator stops processing and destroys the personal data within no more than 30 days of receiving the withdrawal, except where processing may continue on other lawful grounds (part 2, article 9 and part 4, article 21 of 152-ФЗ).

section7.title: 7. Storage of personal data in the Russian Federation

publicPrivacy.clause7_1: 7.1. Under part 5, article 18 of 152-ФЗ, the Operator ensures that the personal data of Russian Federation citizens is recorded, systematised, accumulated, stored, clarified and retrieved using databases located in the Russian Federation.
publicPrivacy.clause7_2: 7.2. The Operator's server equipment and databases are hosted by Russian hosting providers in data centres physically located in the Russian Federation.
publicPrivacy.clause7_3: 7.3. Database backups are also stored in the Russian Federation.

section8.title: 8. Transfer of personal data to third parties

publicPrivacy.clause8_1: 8.1. The Operator does not sell, rent out or transfer personal data to third parties, except as expressly stated in this Policy or required by Russian Federation legislation.
publicPrivacy.clause8_2: 8.2. Personal data may be transferred to the following categories of third parties to the extent necessary to achieve the processing purposes:
publicPrivacy.clause8_2_1: 8.2.1. The payment service “Робокасса” (ООО «Бизнес-Процессинг») — to settle payments for the Services. The following is transferred: order identifier, payment amount, and the payer's email address and/or telephone number. Bank card details are entered by the User directly with the payment service and are not transferred to the Operator.
publicPrivacy.clause8_2_2: 8.2.2. Hosting provider — to the extent required to host infrastructure and store data on servers in the Russian Federation. The provider does not process data independently and acts under an agreement containing confidentiality obligations.
publicPrivacy.clause8_2_3: 8.2.3. ООО «ЯНДЕКС» (the Яндекс.Метрика service) — to collect and analyse anonymised statistics about visits and user behaviour, including “Вебвизор” technology. Processing terms are established by Yandex documents published at yandex.ru/legal.
publicPrivacy.clause8_2_4: 8.2.4. Telegram Messenger — when Telegram Mini App is used and notifications are received through @wesetupbot. Telegram's own data processing is governed by the Telegram privacy policy.
publicPrivacy.clause8_2_5: 8.2.5. Persons engaged by the Operator to support users (consultants and support staff) — on the Operator's instructions and only within the access granted by the user's organisation under “Settings → Consultant”; the organisation can restrict or disable access at any time. Engaged persons must maintain confidentiality and comply with 152-ФЗ.
publicPrivacy.clause8_2_6: 8.2.6. Authorised government authorities — upon a reasoned request, in the manner and to the extent established by Russian Federation legislation.
publicPrivacy.clause8_3: 8.3. All third parties receiving personal data must maintain confidentiality and ensure the security of the personal data during processing.
publicPrivacy.clause8_4: 8.4. Cross-border transfer of personal data to foreign states that do not provide adequate protection of personal data subjects' rights is not carried out by the Operator. If a cross-border transfer becomes necessary, the Operator will comply with article 12 of 152-ФЗ, including notifying Роскомнадзор and obtaining the subject's separate consent.

section9.title: 9. Processing personal data of the Client's employees

publicPrivacy.clause9_1: 9.1. When the Client (a legal entity or individual entrepreneur) uses the Services, the Client acts as the personal data operator for the personal data of its employees and other persons whose data is entered in electronic logs, while the Operator (ООО «БФС») acts as the person processing personal data on the Client's instructions under part 3, article 6 of 152-ФЗ.
publicPrivacy.clause9_2: 9.2. The Client independently determines the purposes and scope of processing its employees' personal data, ensures lawful grounds for processing, including obtaining data subjects' consent, and is responsible for the lawfulness of obtaining that data.
publicPrivacy.clause9_3: 9.3. The Operator processes such personal data solely to the extent and for the purposes specified in the Client's instructions (the agreement to use the Services), does not independently determine processing purposes and does not use this data for its own interests.
publicPrivacy.clause9_4: 9.4. The Operator undertakes to maintain the confidentiality of personal data processed on the Client's instructions and ensure its security during processing in accordance with article 19 of 152-ФЗ.
publicPrivacy.clause9_5: 9.5. The Client is liable to personal data subjects for the Operator's actions. The Operator is liable to the Client under their agreement and Russian Federation legislation.
publicPrivacy.clause9_6: 9.6. Enquiries from the Client's employees concerning the exercise of their rights as personal data subjects are addressed to the Client. If the Operator receives such an enquiry, it is forwarded to the Client or handled in agreement with the Client.
publicPrivacy.clause10_1: 10.1. The Services use cookies and similar technologies (browser local storage: localStorage and sessionStorage) to operate and improve the user experience.
publicPrivacy.clause10_2: 10.2. The Operator uses the following categories of cookies:
publicPrivacy.clause10_2_1: 10.2.1. Strictly necessary (technical) cookies provide the basic functionality of the Services: User authorisation, session maintenance, keeping the User signed in to the workspace, cross-site request forgery (CSRF) protection and load balancing. These cookies cannot be disabled without losing the functionality of the Services. The legal grounds are performance of the agreement and the Operator's legitimate interest in operating the Services.
publicPrivacy.clause10_2_2: 10.2.2. Functional cookies save user settings: the selected organisation, interface display options and acknowledgements of notifications and information messages. They remove the need to configure the interface again at every sign-in.
publicPrivacy.clause10_2_3: 10.2.3. Analytical cookies are set by Яндекс.Метрика to collect anonymised statistics: visit counts, referral sources, viewing depth, time on pages and interface behaviour (“Вебвизор” technology). Aggregated data is used to improve the Services.
publicPrivacy.clause10_3: 10.3. The Operator does not use advertising cookies or cookies for targeted advertising and does not transfer cookie data to advertising networks or data brokers.
publicPrivacy.clause10_4: 10.4. How to manage cookies. The User may disable or restrict cookies in their browser settings and delete previously saved cookies at any time. The relevant settings are in the following sections:

section10.item1: Google Chrome: Settings → Privacy and security → Cookies and other site data;
section10.item2: Mozilla Firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → Cookies and Site Data;
section10.item3: Microsoft Edge: Settings → Cookies and site permissions;
section10.item5: Яндекс Браузер: Settings → Websites → Advanced site settings → Cookies.

publicPrivacy.clause10_5: 10.5. The User may also opt out of data collection by Яндекс.Метрика by installing the official browser add-on “Блокировщик Яндекс.Метрики”, available on the Yandex support website.
publicPrivacy.clause10_6: 10.6. Disabling strictly necessary (technical) cookies will prevent authorisation and the correct operation of the personal workspace and electronic logs. Disabling functional and analytical cookies does not prevent use of the Services.
publicPrivacy.clause10_7: 10.7. By continuing to use the Services without changing browser settings, the User consents to cookies being used to the extent stated in this section.

section11.title: 11. Confidentiality and measures to protect personal data
section11.item1: appointing a person responsible for organising personal data processing;
section11.item2: approving internal regulations governing personal data processing and protection;
section11.item3: identifying threats to personal data security and applying protection measures appropriate to the established security level;
section11.item4: encrypting data in transit using HTTPS (TLS);
section11.item5: storing passwords solely as irreversible cryptographic hashes;
section11.item6: separating access rights: only authorised employees receive access to data to the extent necessary for their duties; within the Services, access is based on roles and access settings determined by the Client;
section11.item7: isolating client organisations' data from each other (multi-tenancy);
section11.item8: maintaining user action and security event logs;
section11.item10: ensuring the physical security of server equipment in data centres;
section11.item11: confidentiality obligations for employees with access to personal data;
section11.item12: monitoring the measures taken and the level of information system security.

publicPrivacy.clause11_1: 11.1. The Operator takes the necessary legal, organisational and technical measures to protect personal data against unlawful or accidental access, destruction, modification, blocking, copying, provision, dissemination and other unlawful actions (article 19 of 152-ФЗ).
publicPrivacy.clause11_2: 11.2. Measures to protect personal data include:
publicPrivacy.clause11_3: 11.3. Personal data is confidential information. The Operator's employees who have obtained access to personal data must not disclose it to third parties or disseminate it without the subject's consent, unless otherwise provided by law.
publicPrivacy.clause11_4: 11.4. If unlawful personal data processing is identified, the Operator remedies the breach or blocks the relevant data within no more than 3 (three) working days and notifies the personal data subject and the authorised authority in the manner established by 152-ФЗ.
publicPrivacy.clause11_5: 11.5. The User must not disclose their credentials (login and password) to third parties and must immediately notify the Operator of any unauthorised access to their account.

section12.title: 12. Rights of the personal data subject

publicPrivacy.clause12_1: 12.1. The personal data subject has the right to:
publicPrivacy.clause12_1_1: 12.1.1. Obtain information about the processing of their personal data to the extent specified in part 7, article 14 of 152-ФЗ, including: confirmation that processing takes place; the legal grounds and purposes of processing; the processing methods used; information about persons with access to personal data; the personal data processed and its sources; processing and retention periods; and the name and address of a person processing data on the Operator's instructions.
publicPrivacy.clause12_1_2: 12.1.2. Request clarification, blocking or destruction of their personal data if it is incomplete, outdated, inaccurate, unlawfully obtained or unnecessary for the stated processing purpose.
publicPrivacy.clause12_1_3: 12.1.3. Withdraw consent to personal data processing.
publicPrivacy.clause12_1_4: 12.1.4. Object to the processing of their personal data in cases provided for by law.
publicPrivacy.clause12_1_5: 12.1.5. Challenge the Operator's actions or omissions before the authorised body protecting personal data subjects' rights (Роскомнадзор) or in court.
publicPrivacy.clause12_1_6: 12.1.6. Protect their rights and legitimate interests, including compensation for losses and non-pecuniary damage, through the courts.
publicPrivacy.clause12_2: 12.2. How to make an enquiry. To exercise their rights, the personal data subject sends a request by email to support@wesetup.ru or in writing to the Operator's postal address: 141065, Московская область, г. Королёв, ул. Ленина, д. 10/6.
publicPrivacy.clause12_3: 12.3. A request must contain: information confirming the subject's relationship with the Operator (agreement number, account email address, registration date), or otherwise confirming that the subject's data is processed; the subject's surname, first name and patronymic; the number of their main identity document, its issue date and issuing authority; and the signature of the subject or their representative. The request may be sent as an electronic document.
publicPrivacy.clause12_4: 12.4. The Operator reviews the request and sends a reasoned response within no more than 30 (thirty) days of receiving it. This period may be extended by no more than 5 (five) working days, with notification to the subject of the reasons for the extension.
publicPrivacy.clause12_5: 12.5. The Operator may refuse to provide information or fulfil a request in cases expressly provided for by part 8, article 14 and part 2, article 20 of 152-ФЗ, giving a reasoned response.
publicPrivacy.clause12_6: 12.6. The User can exercise many rights independently: change account data in the workspace, disable notifications, delete uploaded photo attachments or request account deletion through support.
publicPrivacy.clause12_7: 12.7. Withdrawal of consent to personal data processing necessary to provide the Services makes continued use of the Services impossible and results in termination of the agreement.
publicPrivacy.clause13_1: 13.1. The Operator may amend this Policy unilaterally, including following changes in Russian Federation legislation, the range of Services or personal data processing procedures.
publicPrivacy.clause13_2: 13.2. A new revision of the Policy takes effect when it is published on wesetup.ru, unless the revision provides otherwise.
publicPrivacy.clause13_3: 13.3. The latest revision date appears at the beginning of the document. Users are advised to review the current revision of the Policy periodically.
publicPrivacy.clause13_4: 13.4. If personal data processing conditions change materially, the Operator additionally notifies Users by email or through the Services interface.
publicPrivacy.clause13_5: 13.5. Continuing to use the Services after a new revision takes effect constitutes the User's acceptance of the revised Policy.
publicPrivacy.clause13_6: 13.6. This Policy and the relationship between the User and the Operator arising from its application are governed by Russian Federation law. Disputes are resolved in the manner established by Russian Federation legislation.

settingsWorkloadBalance.title: Employee workload
settingsWorkloadBalance.description: See monthly journal workloads based on actual assignments. Cooks with the same pay should have similar workloads to avoid resentment and staff turnover. Change assignments and journal difficulty to update the table.
settingsWorkloadBalance.guideWorkloadBody: The total across all journals assigned to an employee: difficulty (1–5) × entries per month × average rows per entry. This is a relative measure, not hours.
settingsWorkloadBalance.guideImbalanceBody: Look for a large max–min gap among employees in the same position.
settingsWorkloadBalance.guideColorsBody: The imbalance ratio is (max–min)/avg. Below 0.3 is balanced; 0.3–0.5 is uneven; 0.5 or more is critical and needs rebalancing.
settingsWorkloadBalance.guideUnassignedBody: Journals with no employees selected in their slots are missing from the workload. Open Responsible employees to assign them.

settingsJournalDifficulty.title: Journal difficulty
settingsJournalDifficulty.description: Use this only when the team has no head chef and journals are shared among cooks with the same pay. Difficulty × frequency × rows per entry = workload weight, which the Task distribution page uses to show imbalances between employees. If you have a head chef, you can skip this section.

one.title: 1 — Very easy
one.body: One checkbox, ~10 seconds (examples: hygiene journal, climate).

twoThree.title: 2–3 — Standard
twoThree.body: One or two fields and a number, up to 1 minute (refrigerator temperature, product acceptance checks).

four.title: 4 — Difficult
four.body: Justification, a committee or a formal report (product write-offs, emergencies, deep cleaning).

five.title: 5 — Very difficult
five.body: An analytical document or plan, taking 15+ minutes (audits, training, verification).

why.question: Why use difficulty when there is frequency
why.answer: Frequency shows how often a journal is completed, while difficulty shows the effort required for one entry. Together with the number of rows, they determine the total workload: difficulty × frequency × rows per entry. This makes different journals comparable.

equal.question: What if all our journals are equally easy
equal.answer: Set every journal to 1. Frequency will be the only factor, so workloads will depend only on the number of entries. This is the default approach to an even distribution.

2.label: Easy
2.description: One or two fields and a number, ~30 seconds

3.label: Moderate
3.description: Several fields and an observation, ~1–2 minutes

4.label: Difficult
4.description: An entry requiring justification or a committee, ~5 minutes

5.label: Very difficult
5.description: An analytical document, plan or report, ~15+ minutes

page.title: Incoming VSD
page.proTitle: The integration comes with the Premium plan
page.proDescription: Incoming veterinary documents, one-tap clearance and automatic filling of the acceptance journal.
page.description: Once you have accepted the goods, record the inspection and clear the document right here.
page.bullet1Body: Every 10 minutes we ask Mercury what new has arrived at your sites.
page.bullet2Title: The deadline is one working day
page.bullet2Body: That is how long the law allows for clearing an incoming VSD. We count by the production calendar and highlight overdue ones.
page.bullet3Title: Acceptance and clearance in one window
page.bullet3Body: Enter the temperature, the condition of the transport and packaging, and your decision — and you get a line in the incoming-control journal and a cleared VSD.
page.a1: Clearance confirms that the batch was physically accepted and inspected. Without an inspection it is a signature under something that never happened — and the incoming-control journal stops being evidence for an inspection.
page.q2: Mercury is not responding — what about acceptance?
page.a2: The journal line is saved immediately and does not depend on Mercury. The clearance will be queued and sent when the gateway responds.

autoJournalsPage.title: Automatic journal creation and filling
autoJournalsPage.description: Select the journals for which WeSetup should create a new document for the current period by itself. The second tick is daily auto-filling: every day at 06:00 the site marks employees as “Healthy, {example}” and records days off, leave and sick leave on its own.
autoJournalsPage.pointsNote: Points: {count, number} — each selected journal is created separately for every point.
autoJournalsPage.guide1Body: Tick those that should be created automatically every month or period (SanPiN, HACCP, daily ones).
autoJournalsPage.guide2Body: Every morning the system checks whether there is an active document. If not, one is created for the whole current period.
autoJournalsPage.guide3Body: On the 1st of the month you do not need to create a document for each journal — the system does it. The manager only monitors completion.
autoJournalsPage.qa1Q: What if I created a document manually earlier?
autoJournalsPage.qa1A: It does not duplicate — it finds the existing active document and skips it. A document is created only when none exists.
autoJournalsPage.qa2Q: When are documents for the next period created?
autoJournalsPage.qa2A: 7 days before the current one ends, to leave a margin.

At 06:00 journals with auto-filling get today’s entries: staff journals get health marks that take days off into account, the rest get readings and signatures from the document settings. You do not need to come here every 1st of the month.
autoJournalsClient.automationBody2: Who becomes responsible in new documents and which employees appear in the rows is chosen on the journal’s own page when the switch is turned on. Here there are only the switches themselves.

buildingsPage.title: Points and rooms
buildingsPage.description: Business points (buildings with an address) and the rooms inside them. Cleaning journal tasks are assigned by room — one task per room per day. If there are several points, journals can be kept separately for each one: this is switched on with the toggle below.
buildingsPage.qrPostersHint: An A4 poster with a QR code for each room: an employee scans it and records temperature and humidity without signing in
buildingsPage.guideTitle: How to set up points and rooms
buildingsPage.guide1Body: A café on Lenin Street and a café on Mir Street are two points. Each has rooms inside: kitchen, dining room, washing area, storeroom. Cleaning tasks are assigned by room, and climate journals are printed by room too.
buildingsPage.guide2Body: One point and 2–3 rooms. If there are several points, add each one and switch on “Keep journals separately by point”: documents will be created for each point and a point selector will appear in the header.
buildingsPage.guide3Body: Employees, positions and settings are shared across the organisation. In an employee’s card the “Points” chips limit which points send tasks to them; empty means all points.
buildingsPage.qa1Q: What happens to documents if I switch on the points mode?
buildingsPage.qa1A: Existing documents stay shared and remain visible on every point. From the next period, documents are created separately for each point.
buildingsPage.qa2Q: What if I delete a point?
buildingsPage.qa2A: The point’s rooms are deleted, while journal documents stay in the organisation and become shared.
