compliancePage.title: Journal strictness
compliancePage.description: Journal strictness settings: who can edit already saved entries and when, and what happens when a temperature goes out of range. By default any employee can open their completed task and change the values. The edit history is kept in the journal regardless of these settings.

complianceClient.qrModePublicHint: Anyone who scanned the poster picks their own name. Fastest, but during an inspection an entry can be disputed: anyone could have picked the name.
complianceClient.qrModePinHint: The employee picks their name and enters the personal 4-digit PIN from their card. Five mistakes lock it for 15 minutes. Simpler than a password on someone else’s phone.
complianceClient.qrModeAuthHint: After scanning, the employee signs in with their own account (password or Telegram); no name is picked. The entry is signed by the account — inspectors find this reliable.
complianceClient.readingPhotoOff: Photo capture is off: readings are entered manually, QR forms have no photo button
complianceClient.readingPhotoRequiredOn: Photo is required: a temperature cannot be saved via QR without a photo
complianceClient.readingPhotoOn: Photo capture is on: QR forms start with “Take a photo of the reading”
complianceClient.healthQrOn: QR clearance is on: employees check in themselves, and at the end of the shift you receive a list of those who did not
complianceClient.healthQrOff: QR clearance is off: hygiene is filled in automatically again
complianceClient.qrAuthSaved: QR forms now require sign-in: the account signs the entry
complianceClient.qrPinSaved: QR forms: name + PIN. Set PINs for employees in their cards
complianceClient.qrPublicSaved: QR forms are open: the name is picked from a list
complianceClient.lockOn: Closed day is on: yesterday’s entries are locked
complianceClient.lockOff: Closed day is off: entries can be edited
complianceClient.photoOn: Photo evidence is on: every pipeline step now requires a photo
complianceClient.photoOff: Photo evidence is off: pipeline steps are confirmed with a single button
complianceClient.escalateOn: Management will be told if a deviation is not fixed in time
complianceClient.escalateOff: Only the person responsible for the journal will be notified
complianceClient.editOnlyTitle: Only admins can edit completed entries
complianceClient.editOnlyBody: When on, the “Edit data” button on an already completed task appears only for managers (manager / head_chef / technologist / owner). Regular employees see the entry as saved, with no way to change it.
complianceClient.editOnlyNote: Off by default. Most teams do not need this strictness — an employee who has just filled in a journal should be able to fix a typo themselves.
complianceClient.historyNote: Edit history is kept in the journal regardless of this switch — every change is recorded with the author, time and previous values. This is a HACCP requirement and cannot be turned off.
complianceClient.shiftTitle: End hour of the working shift
complianceClient.shiftBody: When this hour (UTC) arrives, the system automatically closes all “shared shift tasks” (event journals) that have no entries, marking them “closed automatically”. Compliance turns green, but in the weekly digest the manager sees it as a negligence flag.
complianceClient.shiftNote: Default is 0 (midnight UTC = 03:00 Moscow time). For night shifts set, for example, 6 — the shift will close at 06:00 UTC = 09:00 Moscow time.
complianceClient.lockTitle: Closed day — yesterday’s entries cannot be edited
complianceClient.lockBody: When on, after the “start of today” (taking the shift end hour above into account) regular employees cannot change or delete entries for past days. Management still can, but every such action is written to the audit log with the mark closed_day.override.
complianceClient.lockNote: Use it if your business undergoes a HACCP audit and you need to guarantee that a waiter cannot backdate yesterday’s temperature check.
complianceClient.photoTitle: Photo evidence at every pipeline step
complianceClient.photoBody: When on, in a TasksFlow task the employee must upload a photo (phone camera) for every pipeline step. The “Done” button is blocked until the photo appears. Every photo goes into the audit log tied to its step — a manager can look at any time at “how exactly the cook checked the fridge at 09:34”.
complianceClient.photoNote: Turns journal filling from a “bare tick” into a real evidence trail for inspections. The downside is that every task takes employees 30–60 seconds longer.
complianceClient.escalateTitle: Notify management if a deviation is not fixed
complianceClient.escalateBody: When a temperature goes out of range, the message goes immediately to the person responsible for the journal — the one assigned in “Journal owners”. If they have not brought the temperature back to normal and have not written in the journal what they did, managers find out after the set time. One message per deviation, not per reading.
complianceClient.escalateNote: Turn it off if the responsible person is the manager — then the second message is just noise. If no responsible person is assigned or they have no Telegram connected, the message goes to management immediately.
complianceClient.qrDescription: An employee scans the poster of a journal, fridge or room and records an entry from their phone. Choose how the person who did it is confirmed. There is no need to reprint posters when you change the mode.
complianceClient.healthQrTitle: Fit-for-work clearance via the hygiene journal QR
complianceClient.healthQrBody: The employee signs before the shift: no temperature above 37 °C, no signs of infection in them or their family, no respiratory illness or pustules on the skin. Automation no longer marks “Healthy” for them. At the shift end hour, those responsible for the main journals receive a list of people who did not check in.
complianceClient.readingPhotoBody: On the fridge sticker and the storeroom poster the first button is “Take a photo of the reading”: the photo of the thermometer or display goes into the journal next to the value. {autofill} If they do not want to take a photo — “Enter manually”. Turn it off and the photo buttons disappear.
complianceClient.readingPhotoAutofillOn: Digits from the photo are filled in automatically — the employee only has to check and save.
complianceClient.readingPhotoAutofillOff: Digits from the photo are filled in automatically on the Premium plan; for now the employee types them in.
complianceClient.readingPhotoRequiredBody: A temperature cannot be saved via QR without a photo: the photo confirms the measurement was taken at the fridge itself. “Maintenance”, “Repair” and humidity need no photo.
complianceClient.pinNote: The PIN is set in the employee card (“Staff → card → PIN for quick QR authorisation”) or on the shared tablet page — it is the same code. An employee without a PIN cannot record via QR. In public mode the PIN is also asked from those who have one.

consultantPage.clientOnly: Only the client can change consultant settings.
consultantPage.title: Consultant
consultantPage.description: A SanPiN / HACCP consultant or integrator sees your workspace and helps you keep journals. You choose the access level and can turn off the support at any time — access closes immediately.

consultantClient.levelViewHint: Sees journals, reports and overdue items. You make the entries.
consultantClient.levelEditHint: Can fill in journals and configure them for you.
consultantClient.detached: Support turned off. The consultant’s access is closed.
consultantClient.guide1Body: The consultant sends you a link like wesetup.ru/p/name or a 6-character code. Paste it here — you will see who it is and choose the access.
consultantClient.guide2Body: “View only” — the consultant sees but does not change. “View and edit” — can fill in journals for you. You can change it at any time; if the consultant changes the level themselves, you receive a notification.
consultantClient.guide3Body: Does not pay or change the plan, does not delete the organisation and does not disconnect themselves. All their actions are visible in the activity log marked “partner”, and you can turn off the support with one click.
consultantClient.contactViaChat: Contact is through the support chat in the bottom right corner.
consultantClient.noContacts: The consultant has not added contacts yet.
consultantClient.suspendedNote: The partnership is suspended by the platform: the consultant temporarily cannot see your workspace and branding is not shown. The link is kept — once the partner is reinstated, everything returns.
consultantClient.accessTitle: What the consultant can do in your workspace
consultantClient.levelNote: A level change takes effect immediately. At any level the consultant does not see billing or the plan and cannot delete the organisation. They can also change the level themselves — then you get a notification and the event is logged; you can switch back to “view only” or disconnect the consultant here in one click. Their actions appear in the <link>activity log</link> marked “{mark}”.
consultantClient.brandingTitle: Consultant logo and contacts in your workspace
consultantClient.brandingBody: While support is on, the workspace header, the sign-in page and PDFs show the logo and contacts of {name}. If you want to see only WeSetup branding, turn it off. The consultant keeps their access.
consultantClient.detachBody: The consultant’s access closes immediately and branding returns to WeSetup. Your journals and the entries they made remain. You can connect a consultant again at any time — by link or code.
consultantClient.detachBullet1: The consultant loses access to the workspace within a minute
consultantClient.detachBullet2: The consultant’s logo and contacts disappear from the workspace, PDFs and emails
consultantClient.detachBullet3: All journals, entries and action history are kept
consultantClient.detachBullet4: The consultant receives a notification about the disconnection
consultantClient.typo: Looks like a typo: a wesetup.ru/p/… link or a 6-character code is needed.
consultantClient.attachHint: The consultant gives you the link or code. Without one, there is nothing to connect.
consultantClient.notFound: No partner with this link or code was found. Check the spelling or ask the consultant.
consultantClient.ownOrg: This is your own partner organisation — it cannot be its own client.
consultantClient.notActive: The partnership is not yet confirmed or is suspended. You will be able to connect once the partner becomes active.
consultantClient.attachDialogDescription: Access level: {level}. You can change it at any time.
consultantClient.attachBulletEdit: The consultant will be able to fill in journals and change their settings
consultantClient.attachBulletView: The consultant will see journals, reports and overdue items but will change nothing
consultantClient.attachBullet2: The consultant’s logo and contacts will appear in the workspace (you can hide them)
consultantClient.attachBullet3: Billing, the plan and deleting the organisation remain only with you
consultantClient.attachBullet4: You can turn off the support right here, in one click

equipmentPage.guide1Title: Assign an employee to a fridge or storeroom
equipmentPage.guide1Body: Equipment card (pencil) → “Who fills in via QR” → tick the people → “Save”. Only they stay on the sticker; for everyone else the sticker refuses even with a correct PIN. Management fills in any item.
equipmentPage.guide2Body: Print the “QR stickers” and stick one on each fridge. You cannot switch fridges on the phone — the measurement is taken at the equipment itself.
equipmentPage.guide3Body: Type “UV lamp” → model (the lifetime fills in) → “Already used” for a lamp that is not new. The lamp sticker has “I turned it on” and “I turned it off” buttons; run time is counted automatically, and you get a notification 10% before the end of its life.
equipmentPage.guide4Body: Equipment stands in a room of its point. If there are no rooms, create them in “Points and rooms” — they appear in the equipment window at once. When a point is selected in the header, the list shows its equipment.
equipmentPage.guide5Body: For example, a fridge: 2°C - 6°C. These values go into the temperature log as the normative range. The employee sees “out of range” immediately.
equipmentPage.guide6Body: If a Wi-Fi temperature sensor (HACCP/Aubess) is installed, enter its Device ID and WeSetup will write readings to the journal every hour by itself.
equipmentPage.qa1Q: What if I have no fridges?
equipmentPage.qa1A: You can add nothing — the temperature journal will be empty. But most catering businesses need at least 1 fridge.
equipmentPage.qa2Q: Tuya Device ID — where to get it?
equipmentPage.qa2A: In the Tuya / Smart Life app: device → gear → Device information → Virtual ID. More in /settings/integrations.
equipmentPage.title: Equipment
equipmentPage.subtitleByPoints: Fridges, sensors, ovens — by point and room
equipmentPage.subtitle: Fridges, sensors, ovens — by workshop
equipmentPage.stickersHint: QR stickers for the equipment of the point selected at the top — record temperature from a phone
equipmentPage.postersHint: An A4 poster with a QR code for each fridge of the point selected at the top: an employee scans it and records the temperature without signing in
equipmentPage.platesHint: A plate for each fridge and freezer of the point selected at the top: COLD or FROST, temperature range, number, workshop and QR - 4 per A4 sheet
equipmentPage.emptyAdd: First create a room of the point, then the equipment in it.
equipmentPage.emptyNone: The administrator has not added any equipment yet.
equipmentPage.looseHint: This equipment’s workshop is not linked to a point — choose the workshop’s point in “Workshops and areas”.
equipmentPage.emptyPoint: This point has no equipment yet.
equipmentPage.copyIdHint: Copy the Equipment ID (for a DIY sensor or script)

experimentalPage.title: Beta features
experimentalPage.description: Experimental features that are not yet ready for a wide release. Enable them for your organisation one at a time — if something breaks, turn the toggle off and you will return to the old look without losing data. All changes go into the audit log.

experimentalClient.v2On: Design v2 is on. Journals are gradually switching to the new look.
experimentalClient.v2Off: Design v2 is off. Back to the old look.
experimentalClient.v2Body: A unified look for all journal pages: the same modals, toolbars and dialogs. Only the appearance changes — functionality, tables and buttons are the same. On by default for everyone since May 2026 — all 33 active journals are covered, with no regressions.
experimentalClient.v2Note: If something looks odd, turn the toggle off and you will go back to the old look without losing data (the legacy code is kept in every journal as a fallback).

inspectorPortalClient.emptyHint: Create the first link before an inspector’s visit — choose the period for which the inspector should see the journals and get a link to forward.

inspectorPortalClient.revokeBullet1: With this QR the inspector will see an “Access revoked” screen
inspectorPortalClient.revokeBullet2: The printed sheet with this QR no longer works — take it down
inspectorPortalClient.revokeBullet3: Access cannot be restored — you will need to issue a new QR

inspectorPortalPage.title: Inspector portal
inspectorPortalPage.description: View-only access for the sanitary inspectorate / Rospotrebnadzor. The inspector scans the QR code, picks a period and browses the journals sheet by sheet, just like a paper folder. They cannot change anything, and every view is recorded.

mercurySettingsClient.modeOffBody: Incoming VSDs are visible and fill in the acceptance journal, but you certify them yourself in your Mercury account.
mercurySettingsClient.modeAssistedTitle: I certify myself, with one button (recommended)
mercurySettingsClient.modeAssistedBody: The system finds the document, calculates the deadline, sends reminders and fills in the journal row. Certification happens on your button press after physical acceptance.
mercurySettingsClient.modeAutoTitle: Automatically after the journal is filled in
mercurySettingsClient.modeAutoBody: Certifies on its own, but ONLY after a person has filled in the incoming inspection row and marked it “accept”, and only when the volume matches exactly. Works from a whitelist of suppliers.
mercurySettingsClient.unavailableTitle: Mercury comes with the Premium plan
mercurySettingsClient.unavailableBody: Incoming VSDs, one-tap certification and automatic filling of the acceptance journal.
mercurySettingsClient.demoTitle: Demo mode — data is not from Mercury
mercurySettingsClient.demoBody: The Vetis.API access key has not been configured on the server yet, so sample documents are shown. Real VSDs will appear once Rosselkhoznadzor approves the application.
mercurySettingsClient.systemRegistered: The WeSetup information system is registered in Vetis.API
mercurySettingsClient.systemDemo: The Vetis.API key is not configured on the server — demo mode is active
mercurySettingsClient.initiatorLoginPlaceholder: on whose behalf VSDs are certified
mercurySettingsClient.redemptionModeHint: Certifying a VSD is a legally significant action of the authorised person. We deliberately do not do it for you by default.
mercurySettingsClient.noEnterprises: No sites yet. Load them from Mercury or add one manually by its GUID from the Cerberus registry, then choose a location — the site's VSDs will go to that location's acceptance journal.
mercurySettingsClient.enterprisesHint: A site's VSDs go to the incoming control journal of the chosen location. A site without a location goes to the shared journal. Only enabled sites are polled.
mercurySettingsClient.loadQueued: The request has been sent to Mercury — sites will appear here after the next exchange, usually within a few minutes
mercurySettingsClient.loadAlreadyQueued: The request is already sent — sites will appear after Mercury replies
mercurySettingsClient.enterpriseGuidPlaceholder: from the Cerberus registry in your Mercury account
mercurySettingsClient.mapHint: Choose a location — the site will start being polled
mercurySettingsClient.enterpriseRepointed: Site saved, VSDs moved to the location: {count}
mercurySettingsClient.deleteConfirmBody: This site's VSDs will no longer be loaded. Documents already received and the redemption history stay.

mercuryPage.title: FSIS “Mercury”
mercuryPage.description: Incoming veterinary documents arrive on their own; acceptance and certification happen in one window.
mercuryPage.b1Body: Mercury account → “Business entity”. This is your organisation’s identifier in the Cerberus registry and is not a secret.
mercuryPage.b2Title: Apply to join the WeSetup information system
mercuryPage.b2Body: aplms.vetrf.ru — the application is signed with the manager’s e-signature and takes up to five working days to review. We obtain the APIKey as the information system, so you do not need a separate key.
mercuryPage.b3Body: The login of the Mercury user on whose behalf VSDs will be certified. This is a legally significant action, so the person must be authorised by an order.
mercuryPage.b4Body: In a chain, one location may have several sites in Mercury — a warehouse and a production site. An acceptance journal row goes into the journal of the location the site is matched to.
mercuryPage.a1: Not by default, and we recommend leaving it that way. The system will find the document, calculate the deadline, send reminders and fill in the journal row, but a person certifies it with a button. Certification is a legally significant action of the authorised person: if it is done without physical acceptance, the incoming inspection journal stops being evidence. The fully automatic mode is enabled separately and only works after a person has filled in the row and marked it “accept”, and only when the volume matches exactly.
mercuryPage.q2: What happens if Mercury is unavailable?
mercuryPage.a2: The acceptance is saved in the journal immediately — it is our own document and does not depend on Vetis. The certification command is queued and sent when the gateway responds. Resending is safe: if the document is already certified, we recognise that and do not certify it a second time.
mercuryPage.q3: How quickly must an incoming VSD be certified?
mercuryPage.a3: Within one working day of receipt. The deadline is calculated using the Russian production calendar and the organisation’s time zone, overdue items are highlighted in red, and management receives a reminder once a day.

tasksflowSettingsClient.disconnectDescription: The employee mapping and task links will be deleted. Automatic sending of tasks to TasksFlow will stop until the integration is set up again.
tasksflowSettingsClient.disconnectBullet1: The tasks themselves are not deleted in TasksFlow — they will remain there, just without a link to this WeSetup organisation.
tasksflowSettingsClient.disconnectBullet2: If you also need to clear TasksFlow, first click “Clear incomplete” in the send preview, then disconnect.
tasksflowSettingsClient.pageDescription: Automatic sending of tasks to cleaners via <link>tasksflow.ru</link>. Employee synchronisation automatically creates missing people in TasksFlow, and cleaning journal rows turn into recurring tasks for the cleaner. When a task is marked as done, the journal cell is filled in automatically.
tasksflowSettingsClient.linksHint: Synchronisation works by phone number. If an employee already exists in TasksFlow, they will be linked automatically. If they are not there yet, WeSetup will create them in the company the API key is bound to. The phone number must be in the format +7XXXXXXXXXX — then synchronisation will work without any manual tinkering.
tasksflowSettingsClient.noEmployees: No employees with an active account
tasksflowSettingsClient.noEmployeesHint: Add employees in the “Staff” section, fill in their phone numbers, then click “Synchronise”.
tasksflowSettingsClient.failuresTitle: Could not link {count, number} {count, plural, one {employee} other {employees}}
tasksflowSettingsClient.forbiddenIntro: TasksFlow does not allow creating users with a Bearer API key — this is a restriction on their side. There are two ways to continue:
tasksflowSettingsClient.option1Title: Give the key permission to create
tasksflowSettingsClient.option1Body: if your TasksFlow has an API key role with the “Create users” permission, issue such a key, paste it here and click “Synchronise” again.
tasksflowSettingsClient.option2Body: open TasksFlow, add the employee with the same phone number (via “+Employee”), come back here and click “Synchronise”. WeSetup will link them by phone number automatically.
tasksflowSettingsClient.failuresHint: See the exact reason for each employee below. Often the cause is the phone number format or the employee missing from TasksFlow.
tasksflowSettingsClient.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select it manually.
tasksflowSettingsClient.connectHint: Create an API key in TasksFlow: Settings → API keys → Create. The key starts with tfk_ and is shown only once.

tasksflowPage.b1Body: In the TasksFlow admin → Integrations → Create API token. Copy it and enter the base URL of your instance.
tasksflowPage.b2Body: After connecting, the list of your employees and TasksFlow team will open. Link them by matching full name or phone number.
tasksflowPage.b3Body: Once linked, every morning WeSetup sends the day’s tasks to TasksFlow: “Fill in journal X”. The employee sees a push notification in Telegram.
tasksflowPage.a1: This is the employee who verifies a completed journal — a two-step check. It is configured in /settings/journal-responsibles, in the “Verifies” slot.
tasksflowPage.a2: Yes — use the WeSetup Telegram bot (/settings/users → invite). The employee fills in journals directly in the Mini App.

journalChecklistsPage.title: Checklists for journals
journalChecklistsPage.description: For each journal you can create a list of actions (for example “disassemble the equipment, wash, reassemble”). The employee will see the checklist in the fill-in form and tick the items. Required items block submission. All ticks go to the audit log.
journalChecklistsPage.disabledHint: {count, number} {count, plural, one {journal is} other {journals are}} disabled in this organisation. You can still configure checklists for them, but they will not be shown to employees.

journalChecklistsCodePage.description: A list of actions the employee must complete before saving a journal entry. Any item can be made required — then the form will not be submitted until all ticks are set. All ticks are saved to the audit log.
journalChecklistsCodePage.cleaningTitle: The cleaning checklist is configured in “Buildings and rooms”
journalChecklistsCodePage.cleaningBody: Cleaning unification 2026-05-08: from this date the “Routine” and “Deep” cleaning scopes are stored on the room itself (Room). Open <link>/settings/buildings</link>, click “Configure” on the relevant room — it has the full editor for scope/days/products/checklist. The separate items below are backwards-compat with the previous model; create new items through the Room editor.

checklistEditor.noCleaners: The document has no cleaners. First open /journals/cleaning and add cleaners.
checklistEditor.switchedToRooms: Document is in rooms-mode! {rooms, number} rooms × {cleaners, number} cleaners. Click “Force-send to TasksFlow” on the dashboard to see the room tasks.
checklistEditor.roomsModeTitle: The document is in “By rooms” mode — per-room items work
checklistEditor.roomsModeBody: “{title}” — each room will get its own task in TasksFlow. The checklist inside the task is filtered by room (common items + per-room).
checklistEditor.pairsModeTitle: The document is in “Pairs” mode — per-room items are NOT shown
checklistEditor.pairsModeBody: “{title}” is currently in pairs-mode (1 cleaner-control pair = 1 task). For each room to get its own task with a per-room checklist, switch the document to “By rooms” mode. Existing settings (cleaners, controllers) will be kept.
checklistEditor.requiredHint: {count, number} required — without a tick the employee cannot submit the form.
checklistEditor.addItemsHint: Add items — without them the checklist is not shown to the employee.
checklistEditor.noItemsCleaningHint: You can add common items OR bind them to specific rooms — the cleaner will see different lists in each task.
checklistEditor.noItemsHint: For example “Disassemble the equipment”, “Wash the parts”.
checklistEditor.bindToRoomHint: You can create a separate set of items for each room — the employee will see them only in that room’s task.
checklistEditor.deleteDescription: The item “{name}” will be archived — it will not be shown for new tasks, and past ticks in the audit log will be kept.
checklistEditor.monthDayHint: (in a shorter month — the last day)

journalFlowClient.racePro1: Employees see what is free and take tasks themselves
journalFlowClient.racePro2: No conflicts — a task that has been taken cannot be taken by others
journalFlowClient.racePro3: Each person has at most one task in progress — focus
journalFlowClient.raceCon2: Less experienced staff may feel shy
journalFlowClient.sharedShort: Everyone can fill in at the same time
journalFlowClient.sharedPro1: No locks — anyone can take a task whenever they want
journalFlowClient.sharedCon1: Duplication is possible (two people started the same task)
journalFlowClient.sharedCon2: The “one task at a time” rule is disabled
journalFlowClient.manualShort: Employees do not take tasks themselves
journalFlowClient.manualPro1: Strict control — tasks are distributed only by the production manager or the head
journalFlowClient.manualCon1: Employees cannot take tasks for themselves — they have to wait for assignment
journalFlowClient.title: Task distribution mode
journalFlowClient.description: How employees receive tasks. The change applies to ALL journals at once. You can change it at any time — unfinished tasks will continue as they were taken.
journalFlowClient.footerHint: 💡 The mode is shared by all of the organisation’s journals. What exactly to do in each task, step by step, is configured in the <link>“Journal step-by-step instructions”</link> section.

seedAllButton.failed: Could not create pipelines for all journals
seedAllButton.heading: Journals: {total, number} · {summary}
seedAllButton.seeNotifications: See the notifications — they list the journals that need manual setup.
seedAllButton.button: Create a pipeline for all journals
seedAllButton.confirmTitle: Create a pipeline for all journals?
seedAllButton.confirmDescription: For each of the {journals, number} journals (where possible) a tree of pinned nodes will be created from the columns. Journals that are already configured ({configured, number}) are not recreated — your work will be kept.
seedAllButton.bullet1: Employees will be able to fill in the journal’s real columns through TasksFlow right away — no manual setup.
seedAllButton.bullet2: Where a journal has no defined fields, we skip it and send it to notifications for manual setup.
seedAllButton.bullet3: Nothing is deleted. A basic pipeline is only created where there is none yet.

journalPipelinesPage.title: Journal step-by-step instructions
journalPipelinesPage.description: Pipeline instructions for employees. Click a block to configure the steps: which products to take, where to go, what to check. The more detailed, the clearer it is for a new cleaner / cook / shop assistant.
journalPipelinesPage.quickStartTitle: Create a pipeline for all journals in one click
journalPipelinesPage.quickStartBody: Creates a basic tree of pinned nodes for each journal from its columns. Journals that are already configured ({configured, number}) are not recreated. Journals without defined columns will arrive in notifications for manual setup.
journalPipelinesPage.legendTemplateBody: — the pipeline was created from the journal’s columns, basic setup.
journalPipelinesPage.legendTemplatePlusBody: — there is both the basic template and manually added steps.
journalPipelinesPage.legendAdapterBody: — the journal works through a dedicated adapter (cleaning, hygiene, etc.), so a pipeline tree is not needed.
journalPipelinesPage.legendLegacyBody: — outdated JSON format, better to recreate it via 🌳 Pipeline (beta).
journalPipelinesPage.legendHybridBody: — both formats are configured at the same time; it is better to keep only the tree template.
journalPipelinesPage.legendNotConfiguredBody: — the employee will see a free-form entry and the columns will not be filled in.
journalPipelinesPage.hintAdapter: Pipeline via src/lib/tasksflow-adapters/{code}.ts — no separate setup needed.
journalPipelinesPage.badgeTemplateWithCustom: 🌳 Template + {count, number} {count, plural, one {own step} other {own steps}}
journalPipelinesPage.hintTemplateWithCustom: Basic template + manually added steps. The employee sees both parts.
journalPipelinesPage.hintTemplateOnly: Default pipeline built from the journal’s columns. You can add your own steps.
journalPipelinesPage.badgeCustomOnly: 🌳 {count, number} {count, plural, one {own step} other {own steps}}
journalPipelinesPage.hintCustomOnly: Own steps without a basic template. The journal’s columns are not linked.
journalPipelinesPage.hintHybrid: Both formats are configured. The tree template wins in TasksFlow. It is better to delete the legacy one.
journalPipelinesPage.hintLegacy: Old JSON pipeline. Move it to 🌳 Pipeline (beta), which has more features.
journalPipelinesPage.hintNotConfigured: The employee in TasksFlow will see a free-form entry. Create a template — the data will be written to the columns.
journalPipelinesPage.guideTitle: Custom “how to fill in” guide — {count, number} {count, plural, one {step} other {steps}}

journalPipelinesCodePage.cleaningTitle: The cleaning pipeline is configured in “Buildings and rooms”
journalPipelinesCodePage.cleaningBody: For the cleaning journal, pipeline steps (what to clean, in what order, with what) are not stored in the shared pipeline system but on the room itself (Room) — separately for “Routine” and “Deep” cleaning. The employee in TasksFlow will see exactly the steps configured on that room for the day of routine or deep cleaning. This page does not apply to cleaning and is kept for other journals.

pipelineEditor.resetDescription: The order of steps and their descriptions will return to how they were originally.
pipelineEditor.resetBullet1: Steps you added or changed will be deleted
pipelineEditor.resetBullet2: They cannot be restored — you will have to enter them again
pipelineEditor.description: The steps the employee will see when opening a task. The clearer each step, the fewer questions from a new cleaner / cook.
pipelineEditor.introLabel: Hint at the top of the pipeline (optional)
pipelineEditor.introPlaceholder: For example: “Room cleaning. Follow the steps in order”
pipelineEditor.instructionPlaceholder: For example: “The stand in the changing room should have cloths, a bucket and detergent. Gloves are mandatory.”

journalResponsiblesPage.title: Journal responsibles
journalResponsiblesPage.description: Which positions fill in each journal and which exact employee goes into the document header. Changes immediately appear in open documents and in print. Click “Apply smart presets to all” — the system will assign cleaning to cleaners, temperature to cooks, and so on.
journalResponsiblesPage.b1Body: the employees who keep the records. There can be one or several (for committees).
journalResponsiblesPage.b2Body: one person — usually the production manager. Gets a “Verify the journal” task in TasksFlow once everyone has filled it in.
journalResponsiblesPage.b3Body: fills in positions by meaning with one button. Cleaning — to cleaners, medical books — to admin/HR.
journalResponsiblesPage.b4Body: the normal action. Changes current documents + unfinished tasks in TasksFlow.
journalResponsiblesPage.b5Body: a dangerous action — rewrites archived documents and approved tasks. Use it if you are changing things “historically”.
journalResponsiblesPage.q1: Why a verifier if an assignee is already specified
journalResponsiblesPage.a1: Double check: the assignee fills in, the verifier opens the table and approves or sends it back for rework. If you have only one person, leave the verifier empty.
journalResponsiblesPage.q2: Why my admin does not appear in the smart preset for cleaning
journalResponsiblesPage.a2: Intentionally: the admin is assigned only to medical books and audit. Cleaning → cleaners / production manager. This way tasks do not all pile into one basket.

journalTaskModePage.title: Task distribution modes
journalTaskModePage.description: For each journal, choose how exactly TasksFlow tasks are created and how the responsible person verifies them. Cleaning can be distributed by room, hygiene by employee, quality checks by shift. One journal = one summary task by default. If you leave “As default”, the system will pick a sensible mode for this type of journal.
journalTaskModePage.noAreasWarning: ⚠ No rooms are set up in the organisation. The “Per room” mode will not create tasks until you add workshops in <link>“Rooms”</link>.
journalTaskModePage.b1Body: cleaners get N tasks = N rooms from “Workshops”. Each takes their own.
journalTaskModePage.b2Body: everyone gets their own task — for hygiene and medical checks, where “Ivan passed, Peter did not” is normal.
journalTaskModePage.b3Body: Round-robin: a new person on duty every day. Ideal for rotating admin tasks (medical books, audit).
journalTaskModePage.b4Body: Simple mode — one task for the primary assignee. Suitable when one person handles it.
journalTaskModePage.b5Title: A task for each responsible person
journalTaskModePage.b5Body: For committees: finished product quality checks, write-off acts. Each committee member gets their own copy.
journalTaskModePage.b6Body: By default: once the assignees have filled in, the production manager gets one “Verify the journal” task. They open the table and mark “Accept” or reject specific cells.

journalsPage.guideTitle: How to choose a set of journals
journalsPage.b1Body: The set is built from the type of establishment: for a restaurant, the mandatory minimum of Rospotrebnadzor is a few journals, not the whole catalogue. Change the sector and we will recalculate.
journalsPage.b2Body: Recommended journals are off but close at hand. “Other” journals are collapsed: turn them on only if you really keep them.
journalsPage.b3Body: The law allows occupational safety briefings to be kept on paper only. Fire safety journals can also be kept electronically with a signature; we provide a printable form for those who prefer paper.
journalsPage.q1: Why are only a few journals turned on?
journalsPage.a1: This is the mandatory minimum for your sector. You decide on everything else, and the set can be extended at any time.
journalsPage.q2: What happens if I turn off a required journal?
journalsPage.a2: The journal will disappear from the dashboard and tasks, and readiness will no longer be calculated for it. Sanitary rules require these indicators to be recorded: catering businesses face a fine under Art. 6.6 of the Russian Administrative Code of up to 50,000 ₽ or suspension for up to 90 days, children’s organisations are also subject to Art. 6.7 (up to 150,000 ₽ for a repeat offence), and food producers to Art. 14.43 (up to 600,000 ₽).
journalsPage.q3: How does “required by SanPiN” differ from “asked about during inspections”?
journalsPage.a3: The first is a direct provision of the sanitary rules, and you can be fined for it. The second comes from Rospotrebnadzor’s guidelines: the law does not require it, but inspectors almost always ask for such journals. We mark the basis for every journal so that you can decide knowingly.
journalsPage.q4: Why are some journals paper only?
journalsPage.a4: Occupational safety briefings are excluded from electronic document flow by the Labour Code (Art. 22.1) and are signed by hand. Fire safety briefings and the fire extinguisher journal, however, can be kept electronically with an electronic signature; we provide a printable form for those used to paper.

guide.title: How master cabinets work
guide.cabinetBody: A master cabinet is a separate cabinet without journals or kitchen staff. There can be several — for example, “Schools” and “Kindergartens”.
guide.pointsBody: In the right cabinet, press “Add point” — the point starts receiving its menu and raw materials. A point receives them from one cabinet.
guide.operatorBody: Invite an operator by email — a back-office employee or an external technologist. They upload the menu and raw materials and send them to the points’ journals for the chosen date.
guide.codeQ: Isn’t the point code entered in the master cabinet?
guide.codeA: That works too: the operator enters the point’s journal code on the cabinet’s “Connected sites” tab. The code is in the settings of the finished-product quality-check journal at that point. The “Add point” button here does the same without a code.
guide.ownQ: Will the dishes a point added itself disappear?
guide.ownA: No. If the operator removes an item, only that item disappears at the points — what they added by hand stays.
guide.seesQ: Will the operator see journals and people?
guide.seesA: No. The master cabinet only has the menu and raw-material lists and the list of connected points.
guide.moveQ: How do I move a point to another cabinet?
guide.moveA: Press “Disconnect” next to the point in its current cabinet, then “Add point” in the other one. Journal records stay.
